title: The Enormous Turnip
strapline: Pull and pull — this turnip won't come up on its own.
intent: A cumulative story where everyone joins the line teaches that we're stronger together — and that everyone matters, even the mouse.
The repeated 'pulled and pulled' pattern gives children a refrain to chant and a chain of characters to sequence.
Growing, pulling and cooking a turnip links the story to real gardening, harvest and change over time.
Ordering the characters — grandfather, grandmother, girl, dog, cat, mouse — is early sequencing and counting.
The tale is a gift for physical, whole-body play: heaving, straining, tumbling over when it finally pops up.
implementation: Set out figures for each character and a giant turnip to plant and pull, with soil or a tray to grow it in.
Tell the story with a big group heave on 'pulled and pulled', then let children take the parts and add their own.
Wonder together: 'Who should we call to help? Who came before the dog?'
Link it to the real garden — plant seeds, watch things grow, and talk about big and small, more and fewer helpers.
Bring in the teamwork message: 'It was the little mouse that made the difference — everyone helped.'
Let the play grow — children love adding more and more helpers to the line.
key_questions: Who could we call to help pull the turnip?
Who joined the line first, and who came last?
Why couldn't grandfather pull it up on his own?
How does a tiny turnip grow so enormous?
How did it feel when everyone pulled together?

impact.text: Children sequence and count the growing line of helpers and join in the refrain.
Children act out the cumulative story, adding characters and keeping it going.
Children plant, grow and harvest and talk about change over time.
Children pull, heave and balance in vigorous whole-body play.
Children work together and talk about everyone helping.

enhancements: A real growing patch or planter — turnips, radishes or beans — to plant and watch over the weeks.
A giant fabric or papier-mache turnip with a rope for a whole-group tug outdoors.
Story figures for retelling and adding more and more helpers.
A harvest-soup or turnip-mash cooking session to taste what was grown.
A counting line for ordering the characters biggest to smallest.

playing_exploring: Children heave, pull and tumble, playing the story with their whole bodies.
They plant and tend real growing things with fascination.
active_learning: Children keep adding helpers until the turnip finally pops, seeing the effort through.
They tend a growing patch patiently over days and weeks.
creating_thinking: Children reason that more helpers means more pulling power.
They invent new characters to add to the line and act them in.
